package_info.why_malicious: The report provides high-level descriptions of several real-world supply chain attacks (SolarWinds Orion, Kaseya VSA, Codecov) but does not include specific package names, package managers, or code-level details. The macro-level reasoning is that these attacks involved the compromise of trusted third-party software, allowing attackers to inject malicious code or exploit vulnerabilities, leading to unauthorized access, data theft, or ransomware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected code execution during software updates or installation
Unauthorized network connections initiated by trusted third-party software
Exfiltration of sensitive data (credentials, personal information) by legitimate tools
Ransomware deployment following remote management software compromise
file_indicators: Modified or unexpected files in third-party software directories
Presence of unknown binaries or scripts in update or installation packages
network_indicators: Connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs from trusted software
Unusual outbound traffic during or after software updates
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for anomalous behavior in third-party software, especially during updates or installation. Use behavioral analytics to detect unauthorized network connections or data exfiltration. Regularly verify the integrity of software packages and binaries. Employ endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools to identify suspicious file modifications or execution patterns associated with supply chain attacks.
